title: Agent failure diagnosis
summary: Diagnose why an agent stalled, looped, produced invalid output or exceeded its scope, using traces and run artifacts rather than the agent's own explanation.

provenance.notes: The agent's account of its own failure is treated as a claim; the trace is the evidence.

inputs.name: trace
inputs.description: Run trace, tool calls and artifacts for the failed run.

outputs.name: diagnosis
outputs.description: Failure class, the first step where behavior diverged, and a change to test.

workflow.step: Classify the failure: no progress, repeated calls, invalid structured output, tool error, scope violation, timeout or provider error.
workflow.check: The class follows from trace events.

workflow.step: Find the first step where behavior diverged from what the task needed, and read the exact tool inputs and outputs there.
workflow.check: The cited step is the earliest divergence.

workflow.step: Check whether the cause is the task (ambiguous), the harness (missing or noisy tool), the model (capability) or the environment (provider down).
workflow.check: Exactly one primary cause is named.

workflow.step: Propose the smallest change and a deterministic test using a scripted model that reproduces the failure.
workflow.check: The test fails before the change.

workflow.step: Do not retry on a different provider unless the operator authorized that fallback.

constraints: Do not trust the agent's explanation of its own failure.
No automatic fallback to another provider or model.

examples.title: Repeated readFile
examples.situation: An agent calls readFile on the same path nine times.
examples.guidance: Check whether the tool result was truncated; if so the harness needs a ranged read or search, not a larger step budget.

verification: A scripted-model test reproduces the failure class.

task.text: The agent stalled in a looping pattern with repeated tool calls and ran out of steps.
Why did the agent failed with invalid output? Inspect the agent trace.
